propertyEvents.result: Set each job’s estimated cost to complete at June 30 against the costs of July to September and the September 30 estimate
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O15 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O14; the quarterly review’s September 30, 2026 schedule

propertyEvents.result: No job spent more from July to September than its whole June 30 estimate to complete. Three estimates moved by more than clearly trivial, $1,954,000.00 in all. Pier 9 rose $182,000.00 with change order CO-08, signed August 20, and keeps its 9.0% margin. Alder Point rose $576,000.00 for the MRI shielding redesign, priced as pending change order PCO-14 in August, and keeps 10.0%. Tideflats rose $1,196,000.00 with no added contract: its margin fell from 11.5% to 5.0%.
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O15 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O14; the quarterly review’s September 30, 2026 schedule

tape.label: Tideflats Estimate Change, No Added Contract

propertyEvents.result: Read why the Tideflats estimate rose, and whether the cause existed at June 30
propertyEvents.source: 03 After Year End/Tideflats estimate revision memo.pdf
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; the project manager’s Tideflats estimate revision of September 30, 2026

propertyEvents.result: The project manager’s memo agrees with both schedules. The supplier’s 9% price notice is dated August 3, 2026 and the cracked panels were found on August 11, 2026, in panels cast from July 27. Both causes arose after June 30, so the June estimate, prepared on June 26, was reasonable when made and the $1,196,000.00 fade belongs to fiscal 2027, where the quarterly review found it. The job still expects $920,000.00 of profit, 5.0%; a further overrun of that size would make it a loss job. The CPA decides whether the statements should disclose it (WIP-02).
propertyEvents.source: 03 After Year End/Tideflats estimate revision memo.pdf

propertyEvents.result: Costs after June 30 within every estimate · Tideflats fades $1,196,000 after the year end · two estimate changes come with added scope
Profit Fade and Loss Jobs
Compare each job’s margin with its bid and its prior year-end margin
propertyEvents.locator: Jun 30 2026!A8:O14, Completed FY2026!A8:M14 and Jun 30 2025!A8:O13; contract, estimate, cost, earned and billed by job

propertyEvents.result: Five of the 6 jobs completed in the year finished within a point of their bid margin. Corliss Medical Group’s clinic did not: bid at 10.5%, it finished at -4.6%, a loss of $172,600.00, all of it in FY2026 cost. Pier 9 Tech Center, open at both year ends, was 12.0% at June 30, 2025 and is 9.0% now; the catch-up of $406,560.00 lands in FY2026 as a change in estimate. The September 30 schedule keeps 9.0% and the costs since have run within the estimate, which supports it; the schedule gives no reason for the fade (FADE-01).
propertyEvents.locator: Jun 30 2026!A8:O14, Completed FY2026!A8:M14 and Jun 30 2025!A8:O13; contract, estimate, cost, earned and billed by job
propertyEvents.tapeTitle: Margins Against Bid and Prior Year

propertyEvents.result: Look for a job expected to lose money, at June 30 and after the costs that came later
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O15 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O14; the quarterly review’s September 30, 2026 schedule

propertyEvents.result: No active job is expected to lose money: the lowest margin at June 30 is Pier 9 Tech Center, 166 office suites at 9.0%, and after the September 30 estimates Tideflats Cold Storage at 5.0%. No loss provision is needed. Corliss, the one loss, is complete and fully recognized; its $186,935.00 final billing is disputed, which the receivables testing follows. The Juniper Ridge Partners job ($292,500.00 earned) is built for Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, a commercial developer under the same owners, at a 10.0% margin like the others (RP-01).
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O15 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O14; the quarterly review’s September 30, 2026 schedule

propertyEvents.result: No loss job at June 30 · Corliss finished at a loss · Pier 9 faded $406,560 in the year · Juniper Ridge Partners is a related party job
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $103,600.00 of revenue and gross profit, 30.5% of the $340,000.00 materiality, with the same amount missing from billings in excess (WIP-01). The judgments are larger: Tideflats’ $1,196,000.00 fade after the year end (WIP-02) and Pier 9’s $406,560.00 in the year (FADE-01). The other FY2026 areas’ differences are added up with these by the CPA. Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
